title: Snapshot (POST /api/snapshots body)
description: Sender: OpenPairings. The whole tournament as known at one moment, built by PairingsEngine.Snapshot.build/1 and sent as the JSON body of POST /api/snapshots. Headers: `Authorization: Bearer <operator ingest token | installation key orik_...>`, `X-OpenResults-Key: <the tournament's own key>` (optional until the slug is claimed; never inside the body, because the body is stored and served verbatim), `Content-Type: application/json`. OpenResults is LENIENT: it checks only the envelope (`schema`, `version`, `tournament.slug`) and stores everything else uninterpreted, so unknown fields are accepted anywhere (additionalProperties true throughout) and only the envelope is required. The other properties listed here are the ones OpenResults reads when it renders; when present they must have the type and vocabulary given. The prose specification is docs/snapshot-schema.md. Absent and null mean the same thing (not known) unless a description says otherwise. The same document, minus `publisher`, is what GET /api/tournaments/:slug and GET /api/tournaments/:slug/history answer.

version.description: Envelope version. Changes only for a break that cannot be expressed additively. Anything else is 422 unknown_version.

published_at.description: The publisher's clock, ISO 8601. Advisory: unparseable is ignored, the server stamps its own received_at.

publisher.description: Hosted OpenPairings only, operator-token publishes only: the account that owns the tournament. A moderation contact; never served back on a public route.

kind.description: Added in revision 2. What shape the tournament is. Absent means a round-based tournament (Swiss, round robin, Keizer, a team event), which is every snapshot before revision 2. "flow": a Flow tournament - no rounds, whoever is free is paired from a pool - whose games, pool and standings are in `flow`; `rounds` is then [] and `standings` absent. A reader that does not know a kind should say it cannot show the tournament rather than draw an empty round list.

rounds.description: PUBLISHED rounds only; an unpublished round is absent, not flagged.

standings_by_round.description: The standings after each EARLIER round, 1 to standings.after_round - 1 (the table after standings.after_round is `standings`), computed by the sender exactly as `standings` is, in rank order. Compact: each row is [no, rank, points, tiebreak...], the tie-breaks positional against standings.tiebreaks. Never the arbiter's hand-set order. Absent before round 2, for Keizer, for team events and from an older publisher.

pools.description: Added in revision 3. A Swiss that finishes in pools of 4 (the last rounds are small round robins cut from the Swiss standings): the final ranking pool by pool, as the arbiter's own "Final ranking - pools of 4" table shows it. Present only once the pools are cut AND standings.after_round is a pool round; absent before that (the Swiss standings stand), for every other tournament and from an older publisher. Capped exactly as `standings` is: pool games count through `after_round` (always standings.after_round) only, and a withheld player has no row. `standings` carries the same final order as one list, so a reader that ignores `pools` still ranks correctly; `pools` adds the grouping, the pool points and the head-to-head that decided it.

swiss_rounds.description: The Swiss rounds the pools were cut after; rounds after it are pool rounds.

after_round.description: The round the pool points go through; equal to standings.after_round.

pools.description: The pools in order: pool 1 takes the first places, pool 2 the next ones.

flow.description: Revision 2, `kind: "flow"` only. A Flow tournament as it stands: settings, every game so far, who is waiting, and the standings exactly as the arbiter's app ranks them. Players are named by `no` like everywhere else; in a Flow tournament the numbers follow the order the players were entered in and stay put when someone is added.

style.description: normal: plain points. arena: win 2, draw 1, loss 0, doubled while on fire (two wins in a row), berserk +1 for a won game; a fixed end time (`deadline`).

ranking.description: How `standings` was ranked: points (ties to fewer games), percentage (points per game; nobody without a game is ranked), min_games (points, among players with at least `min_games` games; the others follow unranked), arena (arena points). Informational: `standings` is already in this order.

deadline.description: ISO 8601, UTC. No new games from then on; in an arena, the end time. Null: none set.

ended_at.description: ISO 8601, UTC: when the arbiter pressed End tournament. Null: not ended.

closed.description: Why no new game starts, or null while games still start: ended (by the arbiter; running games finish and count), deadline_passed, finished (every game has its result).

games.description: Every game so far, oldest first (the order they were paired). A board number is reused: board 3 hosts one game after another, so `id` and never `board` identifies a game. A game with `finished_at` null is being played.

waiting.description: Free and waiting to be paired, longest waiting first.

away.description: Taking a break: never paired until they are back.

standings.description: In rank order, ranked rows first; this server never ranks. Empty while results are withheld.

id.description: The game's identity for life (the publisher's game uid): stable across publishes, unlike the board.

result.description: null: still playing, cleared, or withheld. A result can change after `finished_at` (a correction): compare by `id`.

finished_at.description: ISO 8601, UTC: when its first result came in. Null while it is being played. Clearing or correcting the result later does not change it.

points.description: What each side scored, in the tournament's points (arena points in an arena). Absent while there is no result, or when withheld.

fire.description: Arena only: the sides that scored double in this game because they were on fire. Absent when neither did.

berserk.description: Arena only: the sides that went berserk in this game. Absent when neither did.

since.description: ISO 8601, UTC: waiting (or away) since. Null when not known.

rank.description: Null for an unranked row (min_games short, or no game under percentage).

points.description: Arena points in an arena, else the tournament's points.

percentage.description: Wins and half the draws per game, as a percentage. Null with no games.

performance.description: Mean rating of the rated opponents + 400 x (wins - losses) / games against them. Null without a rated opponent.

fire.description: Arena only: on fire now (the next win scores double).

streak.description: Arena only: wins in a row now.

no.description: A tournament pairing number (TRF start number) - the only handle that identifies a player or a team anywhere in the document.

swissPool.description: Added in revision 3. One pool of a pools-of-4 finish, its rows in final order.

first_place.description: The first overall place this pool decides.

last_place.description: The last overall place this pool decides.

rank.description: The overall final place, first_place..last_place; the same as the player's standings rank.

place.description: The place within the pool, from 1.

points.description: Pool points: the pool's own games only, everybody starting the pool at 0.

h2h.description: Points among the players level on pool points (the mini-table); null when nobody is level with this player.

swiss_place.description: The player's place in the Swiss standings the pools were cut from.

slug.description: Required: what the snapshot is stored under. An installation key may only publish to a slug minted for it. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; blank is 422 missing_slug.

system.description: Keizer standings carry different columns; the renderer keys off this. A team Swiss is `swiss` with `team_event: true`. `flow` (revision 2) comes with the top-level `kind: "flow"`.

swiss_variant.description: Which Swiss pairing system, beside `system: swiss` only. Absent: not said - every publisher before this field paired the Dutch system (C.04.3). Adding a value here is an additive change.

organiser.description: Who runs the tournament, as the arbiter typed it. Absent when not set; at most 200 characters. A reader shows it as plain text.

homepage.description: The tournament's own web page: an absolute http or https URL, at most 500 characters. Absent when not set. A reader renders it only when the scheme is http or https.

live_boards.description: Only an explicit true links the live boards.

team_boards.description: Boards per match, team events only.

time_control.description: The rate of play as the arbiter typed it.

time_control_minutes.description: Minutes on each clock at the start (first period), for the live boards' starting clock; null when unreadable.

categories.description: The category vocabulary, in the arbiter's order. Present only while categories are shown; never sent as [].

display.description: The arbiter's public-display ticks, resolved: every key a boolean. `flags` and `rating_change` read absent as off; every other key absent as on (`rounds_played`, `performance`, `sex`, `rating_change` start off on the arbiter's side).

hall.description: Hall display settings. Any key absent, out of range or of the wrong shape reads as its default.

registration.description: The entry form's own settings. For the restricting keys absent means no restriction; `list_public` absent means not listed.

amount.description: Decimal string, at most two decimals.

scoring.description: The point system, for explaining a figure only; nothing is added up from it.

series_id.description: The series this tournament is one edition of - the same event in other years. A random id the arbiter's app mints; absent means no series. Not a section grouping: that is `group`.

group.description: The event this tournament is one section of. A block not of this shape is read as absent, whole.

category.description: The one category this player was paired by.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file exactly as uploaded and served (gzip bytes).

format.description: The proof format inside, e.g. ainalrami-pairing-proof.

engine.description: The program that paired this round. Per round, because an update can change the engine in the middle of an event. Absent: not said (paired by hand, by a round-robin table, or by an older publisher).

proof.description: The round's pairing proof, named by digest; the file itself is uploaded separately (POST /api/tournaments/:slug/proofs) when the publish answer lists it in `proofs_wanted`. Absent: there is none.

results_public.description: Absent means true. false: the pairings are published and every result (and points, postponed flags) is withheld as null/absent.

matches.description: Team events only: one entry per match.

board.description: The round-wide board number - also the key Alnasl's live updates use (`round`, `board`).

label.description: The printed board label (team events: e.g. "1.2").

result.description: null: not yet reported, postponed, or withheld (results_public false).

postponed.description: Only ever true; absent means not postponed.

pending.description: Only ever true, beside result null; never with postponed.

points.description: What each seat scored, in the tournament's own point system. Absent: no result and not postponed, withheld, or an older publisher.

rating_change.description: The FIDE rating change of this game for each seat, K x (score - expected score), exact (two decimals at most). A seat is present only when the game is rated for that player; absent altogether when not FIDE-rated, not ticked (display.rating_change), withheld with the results, past standings.after_round, or an older publisher.

kind.description: OPEN vocabulary, rendered verbatim when unknown: pairing-allocated, half-point, zero-point, full-point, absent, vacated-seat, not-joined, not-paired.

board1_white_team.description: The team `no` with White on board 1 (and every odd board). On a bye match OpenPairings sends `false` (no board 1 to have White on); OpenResults reads any non-integer as absent and falls back to team_a.

lineups_later.description: true when this match's boards are held back: the arbiter holds line-ups back until the match starts and it has no result yet, or its line-ups are not confirmed (then `lineups_confirmed` is false too). `boards` and `board_positions` are then empty and the match's pairings are absent from the round's `boards`. Absent otherwise (including a bye).

lineups_confirmed.description: false when the two line-ups of this team match are not both confirmed yet, so its boards are held back (`lineups_later` is then true as well, for a reader that predates this key). Absent once they are, and on a bye.

opponent.description: Absent when there is nobody to name.

kind.description: Absent means played. cut and excluded are sent but not counted in the total.

working.description: Individual standings: per tie-break code, a total and its per-round parts.

rows.description: In the arbiter's order, rendered as sent; this server never ranks.

rank_label.description: The place as the arbiter's screen shows it when a place is shared, such as "2=". Present only when it differs from the bare rank.

rating_change.description: The FIDE rating change over the games these standings cover, exact (not rounded to a whole number: FIDE rounds a rating period, not a tournament). Absent for a player with no rated game, an unrated player, and whenever the board-level field is absent.

rating_k.description: The K factor rating_change was worked out with: the FIDE list's, else B.02 Article 8.3.3 as far as the tournament knows, capped so that K x games <= 700. Present exactly when rating_change is.

withdrawn.description: Withdrew having played fewer than half its matches (FIDE General Regulations for Competitions 6.6): its results do not count and it is ranked last. Present, as true, on that row only.

working.description: UNLIKE the individual table: per tie-break code, a bare LIST of parts with no total - that is what OpenPairings sends. The {total, parts} object is accepted too.
